niche: Practical AI systems engineering, agentic automation, and AI assurance for African organisations.
positioning_statement: LOG_ON helps African organisations turn fragmented workflows into useful, secure, measurable AI-enabled systems, combining automation with engineering and governance rather than selling chatbots alone.

audience.primary: Founders, SME operators, product and operations leaders, and IT/security decision-makers in Nigeria and across Africa who are evaluating or deploying AI-enabled workflows.
audience.secondary: AI builders, consultants, scale-ups, NGOs, and organisations working in low-bandwidth or resource-constrained environments.
pains: Manual processes and disconnected tools make routine work slow and difficult to measure.
AI agents and LLM workflows can be unreliable, difficult to evaluate, or unsafe when given broad tool and data access.
Organisations need practical deployment paths that account for cost, integration complexity, security, and uneven connectivity.
forbidden_assumptions: The audience is not limited to large enterprises.
The audience does not necessarily have large budgets, dedicated AI teams, or always-on high-bandwidth connectivity.
The audience is not necessarily deeply technical; explain implementation choices without assuming specialist knowledge.
Interest in AI does not mean an organisation is ready to grant autonomous agents unrestricted access.

voice.register: Direct, confident, natural, plainspoken, practical, and evidence-led. Avoid hype and generic AI language.
signature_moves: Open with a clear claim about what changed and why it matters.
Separate shipped capabilities from previews, promises, and speculation.
Connect each story to a practical action for African operators or builders.
Disclose commercial interests, weak methodology, and unresolved uncertainty.
Prefer real implementation examples and measured outcomes over abstract claims.
banned_phrases: this is the part nobody understands
voice.person_rules: Use first person singular for founder experience and editorial opinion; use LOG_ON/we only when describing agency work. Address the reader as you. Keep sentences short and make one point at a time.

content_pillars.angle: Design agents around measurable business ownership, professional tools, reliable memory, controlled execution, and human approval.
content_pillars.authority_proof: LOG_ON AI automation work and the user's product/automation architecture practice; specific public case-study evidence should be checked before quantitative claims are published.

content_pillars.angle: Treat agent identities, tool permissions, prompt injection, secrets, audit trails, evaluation, rollback, and human approval as product requirements.
content_pillars.authority_proof: Threathunter360 product architecture and Dial 24/7 Security International IT operations/security work.

content_pillars.angle: Show how APIs, RAG, databases, CRM, payments, messaging, analytics, and UX combine into complete operating systems.
content_pillars.authority_proof: GetUrgent2k, Beame.ng, and LOG_ON workflow integration projects.

content_pillars.angle: Prioritise affordability, low-bandwidth resilience, local workflows, language, trust, and operational realities over imported assumptions.
content_pillars.authority_proof: LOG_ON's Africa-focused automation positioning and Beame.ng logistics chatbot work.

products.name: LOG_ON AI Solution Agency
products.one_liner: AI systems, agentic automation, workflow integration, AI assurance, cybersecurity, and digital product engineering.

offerings.weekly_cta_style: A short, honest first-person lesson from real work, followed by one concrete business benefit and a low-friction invitation. No hard sell, fabricated urgency, or unconfirmed product claims.
